grades.reason: Shows sleep being called inside a while loop that checks for no data, but the figure only illustrates lock overlap to avoid lost wake-ups. It never explains why the wait belongs in a loop.
Describes the RISC-V sscratch CSR, which has nothing to do with condition variables or wait loops.

grades.quote: For this reason sleep is always called inside a loop that re-checks the condition, as in P above.
grades.reason: Directly explains the reason. wakeup wakes all sleepers on a channel, so some wake up spuriously and find the condition false. The caller must re-check the condition in a loop, and accidental channel sharing is tolerated the same way.

Introduces condition variables (wait/notify) and a Java BoundedBuffer whose wait() calls sit inside while loops. The visible text only demonstrates the pattern. It does not explain why a loop is needed instead of an if.
